steps.title: Too many Marcuses
paragraphs: Marcus grabbed Marcus’s skateboard. Marcus told Marcus’s mom that Marcus would be home by six. Marcus’s mom told Marcus to take Marcus’s helmet.
Exhausting, right? Pronouns are the short words that stand in for nouns so we don’t have to repeat them.
Marcus grabbed his skateboard. He told his mom he would be home by six. She told him to take his helmet.

cards.title: Subject pronouns do the action
cards.body: I · you · he · she · it · we · they. Use them for whoever is doing the verb: “She kicked the ball.” “We won.”

cards.title: Object pronouns receive the action
cards.body: me · you · him · her · it · us · them. Use them after a verb or after words like with, to, for, between: “The ball hit him.” “Come with us.” “This is between you and me.”

cards.title: Possessive pronouns show ownership
cards.body: Before a noun: my · your · his · her · its · our · their (my bike). On their own: mine · yours · his · hers · ours · theirs (The bike is mine). Possessive pronouns never have an apostrophe: “its”, “ours”, not “it’s” or “our’s”.

cards.title: The cover-up test
cards.text:
Sam and (I / me) went to the game. → Cover “Sam and”: I went. ✓ → Sam and I went.
The coach picked Sam and (I / me). → Cover “Sam and”: picked me. ✓ → Sam and me.
cards.note: When there are two people, cover the other one and say the sentence. Your ear will pick the right pronoun. Put yourself last: “Sam and I”, not “I and Sam”.

prompts: Explain the cover-up test to a friend who always says “Me and my friend went…”.
Which pronoun pair is hardest for you: I/me, he/him, we/us or they/them?
